steps.text: Sign in to continue to your account

steps.note: W and H are not in the Text section: they live in Position & Size, the section below it, and with Layers, Appearance and an open Effects stacked above them they start below the bottom of the panel. A person scrolls down to read the height, so the walk does the same before it looks, and every snapshot from here on has the readout in it.

the label pinned to 360 wide, which is wider than its words need: it is on one line and H must read that one line's height as a dimmed number, not sit blank. 360 also puts the top right corner handle at a known place on the canvas, 500,140, for the drag below.

the top right corner dragged in to 110 wide so the words re-wrap: H must have grown to the taller number the paragraph turned out to be. The corner is what this walk grabs on purpose, so the number it proves does not depend on the side edges, which resize the box too (`text-side-edge-walk`).

H just took a press and the keyboard landed in it: the height is a field you can set, not only a number to read. Until somebody types a height, it goes on showing whatever height the words wrapped to, which is what the rest of this walk checks.
400 typed into W: the words fall back onto fewer lines and H must have shrunk to the new height on its own
H after the re-wrap: the number must be the shorter one, not the one it read before, because nobody has typed a height into it, and pressing it hands it the keyboard again.
